title.zh: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才
title.en: Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
title.raw: 卷六十八 列傳第五十八 趙知禮 蔡景歷 宗元饒 韓子高 華皎 劉師知 謝岐 毛喜 沈君理 陸山才 Volume 68 Biographies 58: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 58

sentences.zh: 趙知禮蔡景曆宗元饒韓子高華皎劉師知謝岐毛喜沈君理陸山才

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, Lu Shancai
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, Cai Jingli, Zong Yuanrao, Han Zigao, Hua Jiao, Liu Shizhi, Xie Qi, Mao Xi, Shen Junli, and Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 趙知禮字齊旦，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili, style name Qidan, was a man of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, whose style name was Qidan, came from Longxi in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父孝穆，梁候官令。

translations.literal: His father Xiaomu was magistrate of Houguan under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaomu had served as magistrate of Houguan under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 知禮涉獵文史，善書翰。

translations.literal: Zhili ranged through literature and history and was skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili read widely in literature and history and was accomplished at writing.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝之討元景仲也，或薦之，引為書記。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi was campaigning against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him, and he was brought in as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen marched against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended Zhili, and the emperor took him on as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 知禮為文贍速，每占授軍書，下筆便就，率皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Zhili's compositions were ample and swift; whenever he was assigned military dispatches, his brush would finish at once, and they generally met approval.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili wrote with fluency and speed. Whenever he was tasked with military documents, he would finish them at a stroke, and they almost always pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 由是恒侍左右，深被委任，當時計畫，莫不預焉。

translations.literal: From this he was constantly at the emperor's side, deeply entrusted, and none of the plans of the time were made without his participation.
translations.idiomatic: He was henceforth always at the emperor's side and deeply trusted; he took part in every major plan of the day.

sentences.zh: 武帝征侯景，至白茅灣，上表于梁元帝及與王僧辯論軍事，其文並知禮所制。

translations.literal: When Wudi campaigned against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Liang's Emperor Yuan and the discussions of military affairs with Wang Sengbian were all composed by Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Hou Jing and reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the exchanges on military affairs with Wang Sengbian were all drafted by Zhili.

sentences.zh: 及景平，授中書侍郎，封始平縣子。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 陳受命，位散騎常侍、太府卿，權知領軍事。

translations.literal: When Chen received the Mandate, he held the posts of Regular Attendant and Grand Steward, and acted as commander of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen took the throne, he served as regular attendant and grand steward and acted in charge of the guards.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia (560), his title was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，授吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, he was appointed governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, he was appointed governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 知禮沈靜有謀謨，每軍國大事，文帝輒令璽書問之。

translations.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed of stratagems; on every great matter of state and army, Emperor Wen would send sealed letters to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was reserved and resourceful. On every major military or civil affair, Emperor Wen would send sealed letters to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 再遷右將軍，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to General of the Right and concurrently General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to general of the right and also served as general of the van.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Chief, with the posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as attendant-in-chief, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子元恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuangong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuangong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 蔡景曆字茂世，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Jingli, style name Maoshi, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, whose style name was Maoshi, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖點，梁尚書左戶侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dian was Vice Director of the Left Household under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dian had been vice director of the left household under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父大同，輕車岳陽王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Datong was secretary to the Prince of Yueyang of the Light Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong had served as secretary to the Prince of Yueyang of the Light Carriage.

sentences.zh: 景曆少俊爽，有孝行，家貧好學，善尺牘，工草隸。

translations.literal: Jingli in youth was handsome and spirited, had filial conduct, was poor yet fond of learning, skilled at letters, and accomplished in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli was in his youth handsome and quick-witted, known for filial devotion. Though his family was poor, he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 為海陽令，政有能名。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Haiyang, and his administration won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Haiyang, he earned a reputation for capable government.

sentences.zh: 在侯景中，與南康嗣王會理通，謀匡復，事泄被執，賊党王偉保護之，獲免，因客遊京口。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's time he associated with the Heir of Nankang, Huili, plotting restoration; the affair leaked and he was seized, but the rebel Wang Wei protected him and he was spared, then traveled as a guest to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he contacted Huili, heir of the Prince of Nankang, to plot restoration. When the plot was exposed he was arrested, but the rebel Wang Wei protected him and he escaped execution. He then went to Jingkou as a guest.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，陳武帝鎮朱方，素聞其名，以書要之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Chen Wudi was stationed at Zhufang and had long heard his name; he summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Emperor Wu of Chen, then stationed at Zhufang, had long heard of him and summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 景曆對使人答書，筆不停綴，文無所改。

translations.literal: Jingli replied to the envoy's letter; his brush never paused, and the text needed no revision.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli wrote his reply to the envoy without pausing his brush, and the text needed no revision.

sentences.zh: 帝得書，甚加欽賞，即日授征北府中記室參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: The emperor received the letter and greatly admired him; that same day he was appointed secretary in the Northern Campaign headquarters and still headed the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly impressed and that same day appointed him secretary in the northern campaign headquarters, with charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌為吳興太守，帝以鄉里父老，尊卑有數，恐昌年少接對乖禮，乃遣景曆輔之。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang, Chang, was governor of Wuxing; the emperor, considering the elders of the homeland and the order of senior and junior, feared that Chang in his youth might receive guests improperly, and so sent Jingli to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Hengyang, Chang, became governor of Wuxing, the emperor feared that the young prince might breach protocol with the elders of their homeland and sent Jingli to assist him.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，還掌記室。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he returned to head the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chengsheng reign he again headed the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝將討王僧辯，獨與侯安都等數人謀之，景曆弗之知。

translations.literal: When Wudi was about to attack Wang Sengbian, he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu prepared to move against Wang Sengbian, he plotted with only Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli was not told.

sentences.zh: 部分既畢，召令草檄，景曆援筆立成，辭義感激，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: When the dispositions were complete, he was summoned to draft the proclamation; Jingli took up the brush and finished at once, the language stirring and all to the emperor's liking.
translations.idiomatic: When the dispositions were complete, he was summoned to draft the proclamation. Jingli wrote it at once in stirring language, and the emperor was fully satisfied.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷秘書監、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, Jingli was moved to Director of the Secretariat and Secretariat Communicator, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, Jingli was promoted to director of the secretariat and secretariat communicator, with charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，坐妻弟受周寶安餉馬，為御史中丞沈炯所劾，降為中書侍郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother had received horses as a gift from Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong, demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, while his communicator post remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558), he was impeached by censor-in-chief Shen Jiong because his wife's younger brother had accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an. He was demoted to vice director of the Secretariat but kept his post as communicator.

sentences.zh: 三年，武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wudi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (559), Emperor Wu died.

sentences.zh: 時外有強寇，文帝鎮南皖，朝無重臣，宣後呼景曆及江大權、杜棱定議，秘不發喪，疾召文帝。

translations.literal: At the time there were strong enemies outside; Emperor Wen was stationed at Nanwan, and the court had no weighty ministers. Empress Xuan summoned Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng to decide, keeping the death secret and urgently calling Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Strong enemies threatened from without, and Emperor Wen was stationed at Nanwan while the court lacked senior ministers. Empress Xuan summoned Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng to decide policy. They concealed the death and urgently summoned Wen.

sentences.zh: 景曆躬共宦者及內人密營斂服，時既暑熱，須營梓宮，恐斤斧之聲聞外，乃以蠟為秘器，文詔依舊宣行。

translations.literal: Jingli personally joined eunuchs and palace women in secretly preparing the burial garments; as it was already hot summer and a catalpa coffin had to be made, fearing that the sound of axes might be heard outside, they used wax for the inner coffin, while edicts and orders continued to be issued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli personally worked with eunuchs and palace women to prepare the burial rites in secret. It was already midsummer and a wooden coffin had to be built; fearing that the sound of axes would be heard outside, they used a wax coffin instead, while edicts continued to be issued as usual.

sentences.zh: 華皎反，以景曆為武勝將軍、吳明徹軍司。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was made General Who Overcomes Wu and army adviser to Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Jingli was appointed general who overcomes Wu and army adviser to Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 皎平，明徹於軍中輒戮安成內史楊文通，又受降人馬仗有不分明，景曆又坐不能匡正被收。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority executed Yang Wentong, interior minister of Ancheng, in the army, and also received horses and arms from surrendered men in unclear circumstances; Jingli again was implicated for failing to correct this and was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao was defeated, Mingche summarily executed Yang Wentong, interior minister of Ancheng, in camp and accepted horses and arms from surrendering troops under unclear terms. Jingli was again arrested for failing to correct these abuses.

sentences.zh: 久之獲宥。

translations.literal: After a long time he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，累遷通直散騎常侍、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥，仍復封邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jingli was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant and Secretariat Communicator, in charge of edicts, and his fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jingli rose through the ranks to regular attendant and secretariat communicator, again in charge of edicts, and his fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北侵，所向克捷，大破周梁士彥于呂梁，方進圍彭城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, Commander Wu Mingche invaded north; wherever he went he prevailed, routing Zhou's Liang Shiyan at Lüliang, and was just advancing to besiege Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573), the commander Wu Mingche invaded the north. His forces swept all before them and routed Liang Shiyan of Northern Zhou at Lüliang, then advanced to besiege Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝銳意河南，以為指麾可定，景曆稱師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought that with a wave of the hand they could be settled; Jingli said the army was weary and the generals arrogant, and that distant strategy should not be pushed too far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was then bent on recovering the lands south of the Yellow River and believed victory was at hand. Jingli warned that the army was weary and the generals overconfident, and that they should not press a distant campaign too hard.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其沮眾，大怒，猶以朝廷舊臣，不加深罪，出為豫章內史。

translations.literal: The emperor hated his damping of morale, was greatly angered, yet because he was an old minister of the court did not deepen the punishment, and sent him out as interior minister of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated his discouraging the troops and was furious, but because Jingli was a veteran minister he did not punish him severely and merely sent him out as interior minister of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 未行，為飛章所劾，以在省之日，贓汙狼籍，帝令有司案問，景曆但承其半。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was impeached by urgent memorial, on the grounds that during his days at court his corruption was rampant; the emperor ordered the authorities to investigate, and Jingli admitted only half.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, an urgent memorial accused him of rampant corruption during his years at court. The emperor ordered an inquiry, and Jingli admitted only half the charges.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞宗元饒奏免景曆所居官，徙居會稽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized to remove Jingli from his posts and relocate him to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zong Yuanrao then memorialized to strip Jingli of his offices and exile him to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹敗，帝追憶景曆前言，即日追還，以為征南鄱陽王諮議。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the emperor recalled Jingli's earlier words and that same day summoned him back, making him adviser to the Prince of Poyang on the Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was defeated, the emperor remembered Jingli's earlier warning and summoned him back that same day as adviser to the Prince of Poyang on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 數日，遷員外散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，復本爵封，入守度支尚書。

translations.literal: Within days he was moved to Extraordinary Attendant, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, his original noble rank and fief restored, and entered to serve as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was promoted to extraordinary attendant and concurrent censor-in-chief, his original title and fief restored, and he entered court as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 舊式拜官在午後，景曆拜日，適逢輿駕幸玄武觀，在位皆侍宴，帝恐景曆不預，特令早拜，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old custom investiture took place in the afternoon; on the day of Jingli's appointment, it happened that the imperial carriage visited the Xuanwu Observatory and all in office were attending the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not participate and specially ordered an early investiture—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, appointments were made in the afternoon. On the day of Jingli's appointment the emperor happened to visit the Xuanwu Observatory, and all officials were at the feast. Fearing Jingli would miss his ceremony, the emperor ordered an early investiture. Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈太常卿，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was given Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously honored as minister of ceremonies, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改葬，重贈中領軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the burial was moved, he was again given Commander of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (581), when his burial was moved, he was again honored as commander of the guards.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, he was given a place in the temple of Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming (587), he was granted a place in Emperor Wu's temple.

sentences.zh: 二年，車駕親幸其宅，重贈景曆侍中、中撫將軍，諡曰忠敬，給鼓吹一部，於墓所立碑。

translations.literal: In the second year, the imperial carriage personally visited his house; Jingli was again given Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Central Pacification, with the posthumous name Zhongjing, granted one set of martial music, and a stele was erected at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (588), the emperor personally visited his home. Jingli was again honored as attendant-in-chief and general of the central pacification, with the posthumous name Loyal and Respectful, granted a set of martial music, and a stele was erected at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 景曆屬文，不尚雕靡，而長於敘事，應機敏速，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Jingli's compositions did not pursue ornament, but he excelled at narrative, was quick to respond to occasions, and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli's writing shunned ornament, but he excelled at narrative and responded swiftly to the moment; his contemporaries praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子征嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 江大權字伯謀，濟陽考城人，位少府，封四會縣伯。

translations.literal: Jiang Daquan, style name Bomou, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang; he held the post of Minister of the Palace Storehouses and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sihui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Daquan, whose style name was Bomou, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang. He served as minister of the palace storehouses and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sihui.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，卒於通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian he died while Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (570) he died while serving as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 征字希祥，幼聰敏，精識強記。

translations.literal: Zheng, style name Xixiang, in childhood was clever and keen, with fine understanding and strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, whose style name was Xixiang, was clever and quick-witted as a child, with a sharp mind and an excellent memory.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，詣梁吏部尚書河南褚翔，嗟其穎悟。

translations.literal: At age six he visited Chu Xiang of Henan, Director of Personnel under Liang, who marveled at his brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he visited Chu Xiang of Henan, director of personnel under the Liang, who marveled at his brilliance.

sentences.zh: 七歲丁母憂，居喪如成人禮。

translations.literal: At seven he entered mourning for his mother and observed the rites like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he entered mourning for his mother and observed the rites with the propriety of an adult.

sentences.zh: 繼母劉氏，性悍忌，視之不以道，征供侍益謹，初無怨色。

translations.literal: His stepmother, Lady Liu, was fierce and jealous and did not treat him properly; Zheng served her all the more carefully and at first showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Lady Liu, was fierce and jealous and treated him harshly. Zheng served her all the more carefully and never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 征本名覽，景曆以其有王祥之性，更名字焉。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Lan; Jingli, because he had the nature of Wang Xiang, changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's original name was Lan. Jingli, seeing in him the filial devotion of Wang Xiang, gave him the name Zheng.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝為南徐州，召補迎主簿，尋授太學博士。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi was governor of South Xuzhou, he was summoned to fill the post of reception secretary and soon appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen was governor of South Xuzhou, he summoned Zheng as reception secretary and soon appointed him erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 太建中，累遷太子中舍人，兼東宮領直，襲封新豐侯。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, concurrently head of the Eastern Palace guard, and inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he rose to attendant of the heir apparent and concurrently head of the eastern palace guard, and inherited the title Marquis of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 至德中，位太子中庶子、中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era he held the posts of Senior Tutor of the Heir and Secretariat Attendant, in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era he served as senior tutor of the heir apparent and secretariat attendant, in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋授左戶尚書，與僕射江總知撰五禮事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Left Household and, with Vice Director Jiang Zong, oversaw the drafting of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of the left household and, with vice director Jiang Zong, oversaw the drafting of the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 後主器其才幹，任寄日重。

translations.literal: The Later Lord valued his talent and ability, and his trust grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Houzhu valued his talent, and his responsibilities grew heavier by the day.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，每十日一往東宮，于皇太子前論述古今得喪及當時政務。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Personnel; every ten days he would go once to the Eastern Palace and before the Crown Prince expound the gains and losses of past and present and the affairs of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of personnel. Every ten days he went to the eastern palace to lecture the crown prince on the rise and fall of past dynasties and current affairs.

sentences.zh: 又敕以廷尉寺獄，事無大小，取征議決。

translations.literal: He was also ordered that in the prisons of the Court of Justice, matters great or small should be decided on Zheng's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered that all cases in the court of justice, great or small, were to be decided on Zheng's advice.

sentences.zh: 俄敕遣徵收募兵士，自為部曲，征善撫恤，得物情，旬月之間，眾近一萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to send Zheng to recruit soldiers and form his own command; Zheng was skilled at comforting and caring, won the hearts of men, and within a month or so his force neared ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to send Zheng to recruit troops and form his own command. Zheng was skilled at winning men's loyalty, and within a month his force neared ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 位望既重，兼聲位熏灼，物議咸忌憚之。

translations.literal: His position and prestige were already weighty, and together with his fame and influence blazing, public opinion all feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His position and prestige were already great, and his fame and influence blazed so brightly that public opinion feared and resented him.

sentences.zh: 尋徙中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中書清簡無事，或云征有怨言，後主聞之大怒，收奪人馬，將誅之，左右致諫，獲免。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was light and had little business; some said Zheng had words of complaint. The Later Lord heard this and was greatly angered, seized his men and horses, and was about to execute him; attendants remonstrated and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat was a light post with little to do, and some said Zheng had complained. Houzhu heard this and was furious. He seized Zheng's men and horses and was about to execute him, but attendants dissuaded him and Zheng was spared.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，隋軍濟江，後主以征有幹用，令權知中領軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Sui armies crossed the river; the Later Lord, because Zheng had practical ability, ordered him to act as commander of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming (589), as Sui armies crossed the Yangzi, Houzhu, trusting Zheng's ability, put him in acting charge of the guards.

sentences.zh: 征日夜勤苦，備盡心力，後主嘉焉，謂曰：「事寧有以相報」。

translations.literal: Zheng toiled day and night, exhausting his mind and strength; the Later Lord praised him and said, "When affairs are settled I shall repay you."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng labored day and night with all his strength. Houzhu praised him and said, "When this is over, I shall reward you."

sentences.zh: 及決戰于鍾山南岡，敕征守宮城西北大營，尋令督眾軍戰事。

translations.literal: When the decisive battle was fought on the southern ridge of Zhong Mountain, he was ordered to hold the great camp northwest of the palace city; soon he was put in charge of the armies' fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At the decisive battle on the southern ridge of Zhong Mountain, he was ordered to hold the great camp northwest of the palace. Soon he was put in overall command of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, he followed custom and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he went to Chang'an like the other captives.

sentences.zh: 征美容儀，有口辯，多所詳究。

translations.literal: Zheng had a handsome appearance, was eloquent, and investigated many matters in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was handsome and eloquent and had mastered a great many subjects in detail.

sentences.zh: 至於士流官宦，陳宗戚屬，及當朝制度，憲章儀軌，戶口風俗，山川土地，問無不對。

translations.literal: As for the gentry and officials, Chen's imperial kin, the institutions of the current court, statutes and ritual norms, household registers and customs, mountains and rivers and lands—there was no question he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the question concerned the gentry and officials, Chen imperial kin, current institutions, statutes and ritual, household registers and customs, or mountains, rivers, and lands, he could answer without fail.

sentences.zh: 然性頗便佞進取，不能以退素自業。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was rather inclined to flattery and advancement, and he could not make a vocation of retiring simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was inclined to flattery and ambition and could not content himself with a modest, retiring life.

sentences.zh: 初拜吏部尚書，啟後主借鼓吹，後主謂所司曰：「鼓吹軍樂，有功乃授，蔡征不自量揆，紊我朝章。

translations.literal: When he was first appointed Minister of Personnel, he petitioned the Later Lord to borrow the martial music; the Later Lord told the relevant office, "Martial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not measure himself and disorders our court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first appointed minister of personnel, he asked Houzhu to lend him the imperial martial music. Houzhu told the officials, "Martial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not know his place and would disorder our court regulations.

sentences.zh: 然其父景曆既有締構之功，宜且如啟，拜訖即追還。

translations.literal: Yet his father Jingli had merit in founding the state; for the moment let it be as he asks, and once the appointment is complete, recall it at once."
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Jingli helped found the state. For now grant his request, but recall the music as soon as the appointment ceremony is over."

sentences.zh: 」征不修廉隅，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Zheng did not keep the corners of integrity—all was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng lacked integrity in matters of this kind throughout.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞其敏贍，召見顧問，言輒會旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quickness and fullness and summoned him for consultation; his words always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quick wit and summoned him for consultation. His answers always pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 然累年不調，久之，除太常丞。

translations.literal: Yet for many years he received no transfer; after a long time he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for many years he received no promotion. After a long wait he was appointed vice director of the court of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書戶部儀曹郎，轉給事郎，卒。

translations.literal: He passed through Attendant of the Household Department in the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to Attendant, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant in the household department of the ministry of revenue, was transferred to supervising attendant, and died.

sentences.zh: 子翼，位司徒屬。

translations.literal: His son Yi held the post of Retainer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi served as retainer of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為東宮學士。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he became a scholar of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he became a scholar of the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 宗元饒，南郡江陵人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yuanrao was a man of Jiangling in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuanrao came from Jiangling in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he loved learning and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為征南府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liang as External Military Staff of the Southern Campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as external military staff of the southern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及司徒王僧辯幕府初建，元饒與沛國劉師知同為主簿。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat of Wang Sengbian was first established, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei were both chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian first established his secretariat, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei both served as chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，稍遷廷尉卿、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi received the abdication, he was gradually moved to Minister of Justice and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen took the throne, he was gradually promoted to minister of justice and left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初，軍國務廣，事無巨細，一以咨之，台省號為稱職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign, military and civil affairs were broad; matters great or small were all referred to him, and the ministries were said to be well served.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuan's reign, civil and military affairs were pressing, and matters great and small were all referred to him. The ministries called him thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，知五禮事。

translations.literal: He was moved to Censor-in-Chief and oversaw the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and oversaw the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 時合州刺史陳褒贓汙狼籍，遣使就渚斂魚，又令人於六郡乞米，百姓甚苦之，元饒劾奏免之。

translations.literal: At the time the governor of Hezhou, Chen Bao, was corrupt beyond measure, sent envoys to the islets to collect fish, and also had men beg rice in six commanderies; the people suffered greatly, and Yuanrao impeached and memorialized for his removal.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the governor of Hezhou, Chen Bao, was flagrantly corrupt. He sent agents to collect fish at the river islets and had men beg rice across six commanderies, greatly burdening the people. Yuanrao impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守武陵王伯禮、豫章內史南康嗣王方泰等，驕蹇放橫，元饒案奏，皆見削黜。

translations.literal: The governor of Wuxing, Prince Boli of Wuling, the interior minister of Yuzhang, the Heir of Nankang Fangtai, and others were arrogant and overbearing; Yuanrao investigated and memorialized, and all were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Wuxing, Prince Boli of Wuling, the interior minister of Yuzhang, the heir of Nankang Fangtai, and others were arrogant and overbearing. Yuanrao investigated and memorialized against them, and all were demoted.

sentences.zh: 元饒性公平，善持法，諳曉故事，明練政體，吏有犯法，政不便時，及於名教不足者，隨事糾正，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Yuanrao's nature was fair, he was skilled at upholding the law, versed in precedents, clear in the body of government; when clerks violated the law, when policy was inconvenient to the times, or when name and teaching were insufficient, he corrected as the matter required and brought much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrao was fair by nature, skilled at upholding the law, versed in precedent, and clear in the workings of government. Whenever officials broke the law, policy was ill timed, or ritual propriety was neglected, he corrected matters as needed and brought great benefit.

sentences.zh: 遷南康內史，以秩米三千餘斛助人租課，存問高年，拯救乏絕，百姓甚賴焉。

translations.literal: He was moved to interior minister of Nankang; with salary rice of more than three thousand hu he aided people's rent and taxes, inquired after the aged, and rescued the destitute—the people relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed interior minister of Nankang. He used more than three thousand hu of his salary rice to help people pay rent and taxes, inquired after the elderly, and relieved the destitute. The people relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 以課最入朝，詔加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because his administration ranked highest he entered court; an edict added Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because his administration ranked highest, he was summoned to court and promoted to regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為吏部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he became Minister of Personnel and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became minister of personnel and died.

sentences.zh: 韓子高，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Han Zigao was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zigao came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 家本微賤。

translations.literal: His family was originally of low status.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble origin.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，寓都下。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he lodged in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he lodged in the capital.

sentences.zh: 景平，陳文帝出守吳興，子高年十六，為總角，容貌美麗，狀似婦人，於淮渚附部伍寄載欲還鄉里，文帝見而問曰：「能事我乎？

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Chen Wendi went out to guard Wuxing; Zigao was sixteen, still in his topknot, with a beautiful appearance like a woman's. At the Huai ford he attached himself to a unit for passage, wishing to return home, and Wendi saw him and asked, "Can you serve me?"
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Emperor Wen of Chen went out to govern Wuxing. Zigao was sixteen, still wearing his childhood topknot, with a beautiful face that resembled a woman's. At a ford on the Huai he joined a transport unit to return home. Wen saw him and asked, "Will you serve me?"

sentences.zh: 」子高許諾。

translations.literal: " Zigao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao agreed.

sentences.zh: 子高本名蠻子，帝改名之。

translations.literal: Zigao's original name was Manzi; the emperor changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's original name was Manzi; the emperor gave him a new name.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，恒執備身刀及傳酒炙。

translations.literal: His nature was respectful and careful; he constantly held the bodyguard's blade and passed wine and roasted meat.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful and careful, always carrying the emperor's guard sword and serving wine and food.

sentences.zh: 帝性急，子高恒會意旨。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was impatient; Zigao always grasped his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impatient by nature, but Zigao always understood his wishes.

sentences.zh: 稍長，習騎射，頗有膽決，願為將帥。

translations.literal: As he grew somewhat older he studied riding and archery, had considerable daring and resolve, and wished to become a commander.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he learned riding and archery, showed considerable courage, and wished to become a general.

sentences.zh: 及平杜龕，配以士卒。

translations.literal: When Du Kan was pacified, soldiers were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Kan was defeated, troops were assigned to his command.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚愛之，未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Wendi greatly loved him and never let him leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen loved him dearly and never let him leave his side.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗夢騎馬登山，路危欲墮，子高推捧而升。

translations.literal: The emperor once dreamed of riding a horse up a mountain; the path was perilous and he was about to fall, but Zigao pushed and supported him upward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once dreamed he was riding up a mountain on a dangerous path about to give way; Zigao pushed and supported him to the summit.

sentences.zh: 文帝之討張彪也，沈泰等先降，帝據有州城，周文育鎮北郭香岩寺，張彪自剡縣夜還襲城，文帝自北門出，倉卒闇夕，軍人擾亂，唯子高在側。

translations.literal: When Wendi was campaigning against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first; the emperor held the prefectural city, Zhou Wenyü garrisoned Xiangyan Temple in the northern suburb, and Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. Wendi went out the north gate in haste at dark evening; the soldiers were in turmoil, and only Zigao was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others surrendered first and Wen held the prefectural city. Zhou Wenyü garrisoned Xiangyan Temple in the northern suburb. Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. Wen fled through the north gate at dusk in haste while the army fell into chaos; only Zigao remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃遣子高自亂兵中往見文育，反命酬答，於闇中又往慰勞眾軍。

translations.literal: Wendi then sent Zigao through the disorderly troops to see Wenyü, return with his reply, and in the darkness go again to comfort the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wen sent Zigao through the disordered troops to see Wenyü and bring back his reply, and Zigao went again in the darkness to comfort the armies.

sentences.zh: 文帝散兵稍集，子高引入文育營，因共立柵。

translations.literal: Wendi's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they erected palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's scattered troops gradually reassembled. Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they erected palisades.

sentences.zh: 明日敗彪，彪奔松山，浙東平。

translations.literal: The next day Biao was defeated; Biao fled to Song Mountain, and eastern Zhe was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Biao was defeated and fled to Song Mountain, and eastern Zhe was pacified.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃分麾下多配子高，子高亦輕財禮士，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Wendi then assigned many of his followers to Zigao; Zigao also treated wealth lightly and honored scholars, and those who joined him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then assigned many of his followers to Zigao. Zigao was generous with wealth and courteous to scholars, and many men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，除右軍將軍，封文招縣子。

translations.literal: When Wendi succeeded to the throne, Zigao was appointed General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen succeeded to the throne, Zigao was appointed general of the right army and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 及王琳平，子高所統益多，將士依附之，其有所論進，帝皆任使焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, those under Zigao's command grew ever more numerous; officers and soldiers attached themselves to him, and whatever he recommended the emperor employed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin was defeated, Zigao's command grew ever larger. Officers and soldiers attached themselves to him, and the emperor employed whomever he recommended.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjia he became General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjia he became general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝不豫，入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When Wendi was unwell, he entered to attend on medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen fell ill, he attended him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Zigao was given the additional title of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，子高兵權過重，深不自安，好參訪台閣，又求出為衡、廣諸鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Zigao's military authority was too weighty and he was deeply ill at ease; he liked to visit the ministries and also sought to go out as commander of Heng, Guang, and other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Zigao's military power was excessive and he felt deeply uneasy. He frequented the ministries and sought appointment as commander of the Heng and Guang garrisons.

sentences.zh: 光大元年八月，前上虞縣令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反，宣帝在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子，子高預焉，執送廷尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, the former magistrate of Shangyu Lu Fang and Zigao's army commander reported his plotting rebellion. Emperor Xuan was at the Secretariat and therefore summoned civil and military officials present to discuss establishing the crown prince; Zigao was among them, seized and sent to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Guangda, the former magistrate of Shangyu Lu Fang and Zigao's army commander accused him of plotting rebellion. Emperor Xuan was at the secretariat and summoned the officials in attendance to discuss establishing the crown prince. Zigao was present, seized, and sent to the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 其夕與到仲舉同賜死。

translations.literal: That evening he and Dao Zhongju were together granted death.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he and Dao Zhongju were executed together.

sentences.zh: 父延慶及子弟並原宥。

translations.literal: His father Yanqing and his sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanqing and his sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 王琳東下，皎隨侯瑱拒之。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Jin to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Jin in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 琳平，知江州事。

translations.literal: When Lin was pacified, he oversaw the affairs of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin was defeated, he oversaw the affairs of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後隨都督吳明徹征周迪，迪平，以功進爵為侯，仍授都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed the commander Wu Mingche in campaigning against Zhou Di; when Di was pacified, for his merit his noble rank was advanced to marquis, and he was still appointed commander and governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the commander Wu Mingche against Zhou Di. When Di was defeated, his merit earned promotion to marquis, and he was appointed commander and governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 皎起自下吏，善營產業，又征川洞，多致銅鼓及生口，並送都下。

translations.literal: Jiao rose from a low clerk, was skilled at building estates, and also campaigned in the river valleys and caves, bringing in many bronze drums and captives, all sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao had risen from a low clerk, was skilled at building wealth, and campaigned in the river valleys, sending many bronze drums and captives to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，改封重安縣公。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his fief was changed to Duke of Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Jiao was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 韓子高誅後，皎內不自安，光大元年，密啟求廣州，以觀時主意。

translations.literal: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao was inwardly ill at ease; in the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized requesting Guangzhou to observe the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao felt inwardly uneasy. In the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized requesting Guangzhou to test the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 宣帝偽許之，而詔書未出。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan falsely promised it, but the edict had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan pretended to agree, but the edict had not yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 皎亦遣使引周兵，又崇奉梁明帝，士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: Jiao also sent envoys to bring in Zhou troops and further honored Liang's Emperor Ming; his soldiers and horses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao also sent envoys to bring in Northern Zhou troops and honored Liang's Emperor Ming. His forces were very strong.

sentences.zh: 詔乃以吳明徹為湘州刺史，實欲以輕兵襲之。

translations.literal: An edict then made Wu Mingche governor of Xiangzhou, in fact intending to strike him with light troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed Wu Mingche governor of Xiangzhou, intending in fact to strike Jiao with light troops.

sentences.zh: 慮皎先發，乃前遣明徹率眾三萬，乘金翅直趣郢州，又遣撫軍大將軍淳于量率眾五萬，乘大艦繼之。

translations.literal: Fearing Jiao would strike first, they sent Mingche ahead with thirty thousand men, riding the Golden Wings straight for Yingzhou, and also sent Pacification General Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand men in great ships to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jiao would strike first, they sent Mingche ahead with thirty thousand men aboard the Golden Wings straight for Yingzhou, and also sent pacification general Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand men in great ships to follow.

sentences.zh: 時梁明帝遣水軍為皎聲援，周武帝遣衛公宇文直頓魯山，又遣柱國長湖西元定攻圍郢州。

translations.literal: At the time Liang's Emperor Ming sent a naval force as vocal support for Jiao; Zhou's Emperor Wu sent Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to encamp at Lushan, and also sent Pillar of State Changhuxi Yuanding to attack and besiege Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Emperor Ming sent a naval force to support Jiao. Northern Zhou's Emperor Wu sent Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to encamp at Lushan and pillar of state Changhuxi Yuanding to besiege Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁明帝授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔、衡陽內史任蠻奴、巴陵內史潘智虔、岳陽太守章昭裕、桂陽太守曹宣、湘東太守錢明，並隸於皎。

translations.literal: Liang's Emperor Ming gave Jiao the post of Minister of Works; the governor of Bazhou Dai Sengshuo, interior minister of Hengyang Ren Mannu, interior minister of Baling Pan Zhiqian, governor of Yueyang Zhang Zhaoyu, governor of Guiyang Cao Xuan, and governor of Xiangdong Qian Ming all were subordinate to Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Emperor Ming appointed Jiao minister of works. The governor of Bazhou Dai Sengshuo, interior minister of Hengyang Ren Mannu, interior minister of Baling Pan Zhiqian, governor of Yueyang Zhang Zhaoyu, governor of Guiyang Cao Xuan, and governor of Xiangdong Qian Ming all served under him.

sentences.zh: 又長沙太守曹慶等本隸皎下，因為之用。

translations.literal: Also the governor of Changsha Cao Qing and others had originally been under Jiao and therefore served him.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Changsha Cao Qing and others had originally been under Jiao and now served him.

sentences.zh: 帝恐上流宰守並為皎扇惑，乃下詔曲赦湘、巴二州，其賊主帥節將，並許開恩出首。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that the administrators of the upper reaches would all be swayed by Jiao, and therefore issued an edict of special pardon for the two prefectures of Xiang and Ba; their rebel chiefs and commanders were all permitted to show mercy and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the upstream administrators would all be swayed by Jiao and issued a special pardon for Xiang and Ba. Rebel chiefs and commanders were permitted to surrender with clemency.

sentences.zh: 皎以大艦載薪，因風放火，俄而風轉自焚，皎大敗，乃與戴僧朔奔江陵。

translations.literal: Jiao loaded fuel on great ships and, using the wind, set fires; soon the wind turned and burned his own force; Jiao was greatly defeated and then fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao loaded fuel on great ships and set them afire with the wind, but soon the wind turned and burned his own fleet. He was utterly defeated and fled with Dai Sengshuo to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元定等無復船渡，步趣巴陵，巴陵城已為陳軍所據，乃降，送於建鄴。

translations.literal: Yuanding and the others had no more ships to cross; they went on foot toward Baling, but Baling city was already held by Chen troops, so they surrendered and were sent to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding and the others had no ships left to cross and marched on foot toward Baling, but Baling was already held by Chen troops. They surrendered and were sent to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 皎遂終於江陵，其黨並誅，唯任蠻奴、章昭裕、曹宣、劉廣業獲免。

translations.literal: Jiao then died at Jiangling; his party were all executed, and only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao died at Jiangling. His followers were all executed; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.

sentences.zh: 劉師知，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shizhi was a man of Xiang in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi came from Xiang in Pei.

sentences.zh: 家本素族。

translations.literal: His family was originally of plain lineage.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of plain lineage.

sentences.zh: 祖奚之，齊淮南太守，以善政聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xizhi was governor of Huainan under Qi and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xizhi had been governor of Huainan under Qi and was known for good government.

sentences.zh: 父景彥，梁司農卿。

translations.literal: His father Jingyan was Minister of Agriculture under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyan had served as minister of agriculture under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 師知本名師智，以與敬帝諱同，改焉。

translations.literal: Shizhi's original name was Shizhi; because it was the same as the taboo of the Respectful Emperor, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi's original name was Shizhi; because it matched the taboo name of Emperor Jing, it was changed.

sentences.zh: 好學，有當務才，博涉書傳，工文筆，善儀體，台閣故事，多所詳悉。

translations.literal: He loved learning, had talent for pressing affairs, ranged broadly through books and records, was skilled at writing, good at ritual forms, and knew many precedents of the ministries in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had a talent for practical affairs. He read widely in books and records, wrote well, understood ritual forms, and knew the precedents of the ministries in detail.

sentences.zh: 紹泰初，陳武帝入輔，以師知為中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Chen Wudi entered as regent, Shizhi was made Secretariat Attendant in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaotai, when Emperor Wu of Chen entered as regent, Shizhi was made secretariat attendant in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 時兵亂後，朝儀多闕，武帝為丞相及加九錫並受禪，其儀注多師知所定。

translations.literal: At the time, after the military chaos, court ritual was largely lacking; when Wudi was chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals, and accepted the abdication, the ritual regulations were largely set by Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: After the military chaos, court ritual was largely in disarray. When Emperor Wu was chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals, and took the throne, Shizhi set most of the ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 梁敬帝在內殿，師知常侍左右。

translations.literal: Liang's Respectful Emperor was in the inner hall; Shizhi constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing of Liang was in the inner hall, Shizhi constantly attended him.

sentences.zh: 及將加害，師知詐帝令出，帝覺，遶床走曰：「師知賣我，陳霸先反。

translations.literal: When they were about to kill him, Shizhi deceived the emperor into ordering him out; the emperor perceived it and ran around the bed saying, "Shizhi has sold me; Chen Baxian has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to kill him, Shizhi tricked the emperor into leaving the hall. The emperor sensed it and ran around the bed crying, "Shizhi has betrayed me! Chen Baxian has rebelled!

sentences.zh: 我本不須作天子，何意見殺。

translations.literal: I never needed to be Son of Heaven—why do you mean to kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: I never wanted to be emperor—why do you want to kill me?"

sentences.zh: 」師知執帝衣，行事者加刃焉。

translations.literal: " Shizhi seized the emperor's robe, and those carrying out the deed applied the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi seized the emperor's robe, and the executioners struck.

sentences.zh: 既而報陳武帝曰：「事已了。

translations.literal: Then he reported to Chen Wudi, "The affair is finished."
translations.idiomatic: He then reported to Chen Wudi, "It is done."

sentences.zh: 」武帝曰：「卿乃忠於我，後莫復爾。

translations.literal: " Wudi said, "You have been loyal to me; do not do this again."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi said, "You have been loyal to me. Do not do this again."

sentences.zh: 」師知不對。

translations.literal: " Shizhi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，仍兼舍人。

translations.literal: When Wudi received the Mandate, he still concurrently served as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Shizhi still served as attendant.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，與物多忤，雖位宦不遷，而任遇甚重，其所獻替，皆有弘益。

translations.literal: His nature was loose and simple; he clashed with many people. Though his official rank did not advance, his trust and favor were very weighty, and what he offered and replaced all brought broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and unceremonious and often clashed with others. Though his rank did not advance, his trust and responsibilities were great, and his counsel brought broad benefit.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，六日成服，時朝臣共議大行皇帝靈座俠御人衣服吉凶之制，博士沈文阿議宜服吉，師知議云：「既稱成服，本備喪禮。

translations.literal: When Wudi died, on the sixth day they completed mourning garments. At the time the court ministers jointly discussed whether the attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress; Erudite Shen Wen'a argued they should wear auspicious dress. Shizhi argued, "Since it is called completing mourning garments, it fundamentally prepares funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, mourning garments were completed on the sixth day. The court debated whether attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress. Erudite Shen Wen'a argued for auspicious dress. Shizhi argued, "Since this is called completing mourning garments, it is fundamentally a funeral rite.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，成服，俠侍之官，悉著衰斬，唯著鎧不異，此即可擬。

translations.literal: According to the case when Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming died, when mourning garments were completed, the attendants all wore hemp mourning, differing only in wearing armor—this may be taken as a parallel."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the attendants all wore hemp mourning when mourning garments were completed, differing only in wearing armor. This precedent applies."

sentences.zh: 愚謂六日成服，俠靈座須服衰絰。

translations.literal: I hold that on the sixth day when mourning garments are completed, those attending the spirit seat must wear hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the sixth day, attendants at the spirit seat must wear hemp mourning."

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人蔡景曆、江德藻、謝岐等同師知議。

translations.literal: " Secretariat Attendants Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others agreed with Shizhi's view.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat attendants Cai Jingli, Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others agreed with Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 時以二議不同，乃啟取左丞徐陵決斷。

translations.literal: As the two views differed, they memorialized to have Left Vice Director Xu Ling decide.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two views differed, they memorialized to have left vice director Xu Ling decide.

sentences.zh: 陵云：「案山陵鹵簿吉部伍中，公卿以下導引者，爰及武賁、鼓吹、執蓋、奉車，並是吉服，豈容俠禦獨為衰絰？

translations.literal: Ling said, "According to the auspicious section of the funeral procession for the mountain tomb, from dukes and ministers down, those who lead, as well as the martial guards, martial music, canopy bearers, and carriage attendants—all wear auspicious dress. How can the attendants alone wear hemp mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Ling said, "In the auspicious section of the funeral procession for the imperial tomb, from dukes and ministers down through martial guards, martial music, canopy bearers, and carriage attendants, all wear auspicious dress. How can the attendants alone wear hemp mourning?

sentences.zh: 若言公卿胥吏並服衰絰，此與梓宮部伍有何差別？

translations.literal: If one says that dukes, ministers, clerks, and officers all wear hemp mourning, what difference is there from the catafalque procession?
translations.idiomatic: If dukes, ministers, clerks, and officers all wore hemp mourning, what difference would there be from the catafalque procession?

sentences.zh: 若言文物並吉，司事者凶，豈容衽絰而奉華蓋，衰衣而升玉路邪？

translations.literal: If one says the ritual objects are all auspicious while those who perform the rites are inauspicious, how can one wear hemp sashes while holding the flowered canopy, or mourning robes while mounting the jade carriage?"
translations.idiomatic: If the ritual objects are auspicious while those who perform the rites are inauspicious, how can one wear hemp sashes while holding the flowered canopy, or mourning robes while mounting the jade carriage?"

sentences.zh: 同博士議。

translations.literal: He agreed with the erudite's view.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed with the erudite.

sentences.zh: 」謝岐議曰：「靈筵祔宗廟，梓宮祔山陵，實如左丞議。

translations.literal: " Xie Qi argued, "The spirit seat is enshrined in the ancestral temple and the catafalque in the mountain tomb—this is indeed as the Left Vice Director says.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi argued, "The spirit seat is enshrined in the ancestral temple and the catafalque in the imperial tomb, as the left vice director says.

sentences.zh: 但山陵鹵簿，備有吉凶，從靈輿者儀服無變，從梓宮者皆服苴衰，爰至士禮，悉同此制。

translations.literal: But the funeral procession for the mountain tomb has both auspicious and inauspicious elements; those following the spirit carriage keep their dress unchanged, while those following the catafalque all wear coarse hemp mourning—even down to commoner rites, all follow this rule.
translations.idiomatic: But the funeral procession has both auspicious and inauspicious elements. Those following the spirit carriage keep their dress unchanged, while those following the catafalque all wear coarse hemp mourning. Even commoner rites follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 此自是山陵之儀，非關成服。

translations.literal: This is itself the rite of the mountain tomb and is not connected with completing mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: This belongs to the tomb rites and is not connected with completing mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 今謂梓宮靈扆，共在西階，稱為成服，亦無鹵簿，直是爰自胥吏，上至王公，四海之內，必備衰絰。

translations.literal: Now it is said that the catafalque and spirit seat are together on the western steps; called completing mourning garments, there is also no procession—simply from clerks up to princes and dukes, within the four seas, all must prepare hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the catafalque and spirit seat stand together on the western steps. Called completing mourning garments, there is no procession—simply from clerks up to princes and dukes, all within the realm must wear hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，略是成例，豈容凡百士庶，悉皆服重，而侍中至於武衛，最是近官，反鳴玉紆青，與平吉不異？

translations.literal: According to the case when Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming died, this is roughly the established precedent. How can common scholars and commoners all wear heavy mourning, while attendants-in-chief down to the martial guard—the closest officials—instead jingle jade and wear green, no different from ordinary auspicious days?
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, this was roughly the precedent. How can common scholars and commoners all wear heavy mourning while attendants-in-chief down to the martial guard—the closest officials—wear jade and green robes no different from ordinary auspicious days?

sentences.zh: 左丞既推以山陵事，愚意或謂與成服有殊。

translations.literal: Since the Left Vice Director has argued from the matter of the mountain tomb, in my humble view this may differ from completing mourning garments."
translations.idiomatic: Since the left vice director argued from the tomb rites, in my view this may differ from completing mourning garments."

sentences.zh: 」陵重答云：「老病屬纊，不能多說。

translations.literal: " Ling replied again, "Old and ill, I am near death's curtain and cannot say much.
translations.idiomatic: Ling replied again, "Old and ill, I am near death and cannot say much.

sentences.zh: 古人爭議，多成怨府，傅玄見尤于晉代，王商取陷於漢朝。

translations.literal: When men of old disputed, they often became houses of resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in the Jin, Wang Shang was trapped in the Han.
translations.idiomatic: When men of old disputed ritual, they often made lasting enemies. Fu Xuan was blamed in Jin times, Wang Shang was ruined in Han times.

sentences.zh: 謹自三緘，敬同高命。

translations.literal: I respectfully seal my lips thrice and defer to your lofty command.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hold my tongue and defer to your command.

sentences.zh: 若萬一不死，猶得展言，庶與群賢，更申揚榷。

translations.literal: If by any chance I do not die, I may yet speak at length and, with the assembled worthies, discuss further.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance I do not die, I may yet speak further and discuss the matter again with the assembled worthies."

sentences.zh: 」文阿猶執所見，眾議不能決，乃具錄二議奏聞，上從師知議。

translations.literal: " Wen'a still held to his view; the assembly could not decide, so they fully recorded both views and memorialized; the emperor followed Shizhi's view.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'a still held to his view. The assembly could not decide, so both views were recorded and memorialized. The emperor followed Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Guests, his attendant post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of guests while retaining his post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋起為中書舍人，復掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised again as Secretariat Attendant and again in charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed secretariat attendant and again put in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，文帝不豫，師知與尚書僕射到仲舉等入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, when Wendi was unwell, Shizhi with Vice Director of the Secretariat Dao Zhongju and others entered to attend on medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang, when Emperor Wen fell ill, Shizhi with vice director Dao Zhongju and others attended him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，豫顧命。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he was included in the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Shizhi was named in the final testament.

sentences.zh: 宣帝入輔，師知與仲舉等遣舍人殷不佞矯詔令宣帝還東府，事覺，於北獄賜死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Shizhi with Zhongju and others sent Attendant Yin Buren with a forged edict ordering Xuan back to the Eastern Residence; when the affair was exposed, he was granted death in the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Shizhi with Zhongju and others sent attendant Yin Buren with a forged edict ordering Xuan back to the eastern residence. When the plot was exposed, he was executed in the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝敕師知撰起居注，自永定二年秋至天嘉元年為十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wendi ordered Shizhi to compile the Diary of Activity and Repose, from autumn of the second year of Yongding to the first year of Tianjia, ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wen ordered Shizhi to compile the diary of activity and repose from autumn of the second year of Yongding through the first year of Tianjia, ten juan in all.

sentences.zh: 謝岐，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Qi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父達，梁太學博士。

translations.literal: His father Da was Erudite of the Imperial Academy under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da had been erudite of the imperial academy under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 弟嶠，篤學，為通儒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and became a comprehensive scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qiao was devoted to learning and became a comprehensive scholar.

sentences.zh: 毛喜字伯武，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xi, style name Bowu, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi, whose style name was Bowu, came from Yangwu in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖稱，梁散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Regular Attendant under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had been regular attendant under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父棲忠，中權司馬。

translations.literal: His father Qizhong was Marshal of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qizhong had been marshal of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗謂宣帝曰：「我諸子皆以'伯'為名，汝諸子宜用'叔'為稱。

translations.literal: Wendi once said to Emperor Xuan, "All my sons take 'bo' in their names; your sons should use 'shu' as their designation."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan, "All my sons take bo in their names; your sons should use shu in theirs."

sentences.zh: 」宣帝以訪喜，喜即條自古名賢杜叔英、虞叔卿等二十餘人以啟之，文帝稱善。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of old such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and presented them; Wendi praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi. Xi promptly listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and presented the list. Emperor Wen approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，廢帝沖昧，宣帝錄尚書輔政，僕射到仲舉等矯太后令，遣宣帝還東府，當時疑懼，無敢厝言。

translations.literal: When Wendi died, the Deposed Emperor was young and dim; Emperor Xuan recorded affairs of the Secretariat as regent. Vice Director Dao Zhongju and others forged the empress dowager's order sending Xuan back to the Eastern Residence; at the time all were fearful and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the deposed emperor was young and inexperienced. Emperor Xuan took charge of the secretariat as regent. Vice director Dao Zhongju and others forged the empress dowager's order sending Xuan back to the eastern residence. All were fearful and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 喜即馳入，謂宣帝曰：「今日之言，必非太后之意，宗社至重，願加三思。

translations.literal: Xi at once rushed in and said to Emperor Xuan, "Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent; the altars of state are supremely weighty—I beg you to think thrice."
translations.idiomatic: Xi rushed in at once and told Emperor Xuan, "Today's order surely does not come from the empress dowager. The fate of the state is at stake—I beg you to think again."

sentences.zh: 」竟如其策。

translations.literal: " In the end it was as he had advised.
translations.idiomatic: In the end events unfolded as he had advised.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍韓子高始與仲舉通謀，其事未發，喜謂宣帝曰：「宜簡人馬配與子高，並賜鐵炭，使修器甲。

translations.literal: General of the Right Guard Han Zigao had at first plotted with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken out. Xi said to Emperor Xuan, "You should select men and horses to assign to Zigao, and also grant him iron and charcoal to have him repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: General of the right guard Han Zigao had at first plotted with Zhongju, though the plot had not yet broken out. Xi told Emperor Xuan, "You should assign men and horses to Zigao and grant him iron and charcoal to repair weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 」宣帝曰：「子高即欲收執，何更如是？

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuan said, "Zigao is about to be seized and arrested—why do this further?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said, "I am about to arrest Zigao—why do this?"

sentences.zh: 」喜曰：「山陵始畢，邊寇尚多，而子高受委前朝，名為杖順，宜推心安誘，使不自疑，圖之一壯士之力耳。

translations.literal: " Xi said, "The mountain tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many, while Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as upholding obedience. You should reassure him and win him over so that he does not suspect himself—seizing him is but the strength of one brave man."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The imperial tomb rites have only just ended and border enemies are still numerous. Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as loyal. You should reassure and win him over so he does not grow suspicious. Arresting him would take only one brave man's effort."

sentences.zh: 」宣帝卒行其計。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuan in the end carried out his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan carried out his plan.

sentences.zh: 及得淮南之地，喜陳安邊之術，宣帝納之，即日施行。

translations.literal: When they gained the lands of Huainan, Xi presented methods for securing the borders; Emperor Xuan accepted them and implemented them that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When they gained the Huainan region, Xi presented methods for securing the borders. Emperor Xuan accepted them and implemented them that same day.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲進兵彭、汴，以問喜，喜以為「淮左新平，邊人未輯，周氏始吞齊國，難與爭鋒，未若安人保境，斯久長之術也」。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to advance troops to Peng and Bian and consulted Xi; Xi held that "the left bank of the Huai is newly pacified and the border people are not yet settled; the Zhou have just swallowed Qi and are hard to contend with—it is better to settle the people and guard the borders; this is the method of long endurance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to advance on Peng and Bian and consulted Xi. Xi argued, "The Huai region is newly pacified and the border people are not yet settled. Northern Zhou has just swallowed Qi and would be hard to fight. It is better to settle the people and guard the borders—that is the strategy for long survival."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹卒俘于周。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche in the end was captured by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche was eventually captured by Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 喜後曆丹陽尹，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xi later passed through the posts of governor of Danyang and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xi later served as governor of Danyang and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，叔陵構逆，敕中庶子陸瓊宣旨，令南北諸軍皆取喜處分。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted rebellion; an edict ordered Senior Tutor Lu Qiong to proclaim the decree, directing all armies north and south to take Xi's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted rebellion. An edict ordered senior tutor Lu Qiong to proclaim that all armies north and south were to follow Xi's orders.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加侍中。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was given Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, he was given the additional title of attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝委政於喜，喜數有諫爭，事並見從。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi repeatedly remonstrated and argued, and his matters were all followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi. Xi repeatedly remonstrated, and his advice was followed.

sentences.zh: 自明徹敗後，帝深悔不用其言，謂袁憲曰：「一不用喜計，遂令至此。

translations.literal: After Mingche's defeat, the emperor deeply regretted not using his words and said to Yuan Xian, "Had I not used Xi's plan even once, it brought us to this."
translations.idiomatic: After Mingche's defeat, the emperor deeply regretted ignoring Xi's advice and told Yuan Xian, "If I had followed Xi's plan even once, we would not be in this plight."

sentences.zh: 」由是益見親重，喜乃言無回避。

translations.literal: " From this he was all the more seen as intimate and weighty, and Xi then spoke without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xi was all the more trusted and spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子好酒德，每共親幸人為長夜之宴，喜嘗言之宣帝，太子遂銜之，即位後稍見疏遠。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince was fond of wine and virtue; he often held all-night feasts with his intimate favorites. Xi once spoke of this to Emperor Xuan, and the prince therefore harbored resentment; after taking the throne he gradually grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was fond of wine and often held all-night feasts with his favorites. Xi once reported this to Emperor Xuan, and the prince bore a grudge. After he took the throne, Xi was gradually distanced.

sentences.zh: 及被始興王傷，創愈，置酒引江總以下，展樂賦詩，醉酣而命喜。

translations.literal: When he was wounded by the Prince of Shixing and his wounds healed, he set out wine and summoned Jiang Zong and those below, spreading music and composing poems; drunk and flushed, he summoned Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After he was wounded by the Prince of Shixing and recovered, he held a feast for Jiang Zong and others, with music and poetry. Drunk, he summoned Xi.

sentences.zh: 于時山陵初畢，未及踰年，喜見之不懌，欲諫而後主已醉。

translations.literal: At the time the mountain tomb had only just been completed and a year had not yet passed; Xi saw this and was displeased, wishing to remonstrate but the Later Lord was already drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb rites had only just ended and a year had not yet passed. Xi was displeased and wished to remonstrate, but Houzhu was already drunk.

sentences.zh: 喜言心疾，僕於階下，移出省中。

translations.literal: Xi claimed heart illness, collapsed on the steps, and was moved out of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi claimed heart trouble, collapsed on the steps, and was carried out of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後主醒，乃謂江總曰：「我悔召毛喜，知其無病，但欲阻我歡宴，非我所為耳。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord awoke, he then said to Jiang Zong, "I regret summoning Mao Xi; I know he has no illness—he only wished to obstruct my merry feast. This is not what I would do."
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu awoke, he told Jiang Zong, "I regret summoning Mao Xi. I know he is not ill—he only wanted to spoil my feast. That is not what I would do."

sentences.zh: 」乃與司馬申謀曰：「此人負氣，吾欲將乞鄱陽兄弟，聽其報讎，可乎？

translations.literal: " He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying, "This man is proud in spirit; I wish to send him to beg the brothers of Poyang and let him take revenge—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with Sima Shen and said, "This man is proud. I wish to send him to the brothers of Poyang and let him take revenge on the Prince of Shixing—would that do?"

sentences.zh: 「對曰：「終不為官用，願如聖旨。

translations.literal: " The reply was, "He will never serve in office again; let it be as Your Majesty decrees."
translations.idiomatic: Shen replied, "He will never serve in office again. Let it be as Your Majesty decrees."

sentences.zh: 」傅縡爭之曰：「若許報讎，欲置先皇何地？

translations.literal: " Fu Yi argued, "If revenge is permitted, where would you place the late emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi objected, "If you permit revenge, where does that leave the late emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」後主曰：「當與一小郡，勿令見人事耳。」

translations.literal: " The Later Lord said, "He shall be given a small commandery and not allowed to see human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "Give him a small commandery and keep him from court affairs."

sentences.zh: 至德元年，授永嘉內史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed interior minister of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed interior minister of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 喜至郡，不受奉秩，政弘清靜，人吏安之。

translations.literal: When Xi reached the commandery he did not accept salary and stipend; his government was broad and clear and quiet, and the people and clerks were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached his post he refused his salary. His government was clear and quiet, and the people and officials were content.

sentences.zh: 遇豐州刺史章大寶舉兵反，郡與豐州接，而素無備，喜乃修城隍器械，又遣兵援建安。

translations.literal: When the governor of Fengzhou Zhang Dabao raised troops in rebellion, the commandery bordered Fengzhou and had long been unprepared; Xi therefore repaired walls, moats, and weapons, and also sent troops to aid Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor of Fengzhou Zhang Dabao rebelled, Yongjia bordered Fengzhou and was unprepared. Xi repaired the walls and weapons and sent troops to aid Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授南安內史。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed interior minister of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, he was appointed interior minister of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，徵為光祿大夫，領左驍騎將軍，道卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming he was summoned as grand master of splendid happiness and general of the left valiant cavalry, and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子處沖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chuchong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuchong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 沈君理字仲倫，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Shen Junli, style name Zhonglun, was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Junli, whose style name was Zhonglun, came from Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖僧畟，梁左戶尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengbi was Minister of the Left Household under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbi had been minister of the left household under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父巡，元帝時位少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Xun held the post of Minister of the Palace Storehouses under Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had served as minister of the palace storehouses under Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 魏平荊州，梁宣帝署金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jingzhou, Liang's Emperor Xuan appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
