translations.idiomatic: When Wei pacified Jingzhou, Emperor Xuan of Liang appointed him grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 君理美風儀，博涉有識鑒。

translations.literal: Junli had fine bearing and manner, ranged broadly and had discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Junli had fine bearing and manners, read widely, and showed keen discernment.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝鎮南徐州，巡遣君理致謁，深見器重，命尚會稽長公主。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi was stationed at South Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay respects; he was deeply esteemed and ordered to marry the Elder Princess of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen was stationed at South Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli to pay his respects. Wu greatly valued him and had him marry the elder princess of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，拜駙馬都尉，封永安亭侯，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an Pavilion, and made governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he was appointed commandant of the horse guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an Pavilion, and made governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 時兵革未甯，百姓荒弊，君理總集士卒，修飾器械，深以幹理見稱。

translations.literal: At the time the weapons of war were not yet stilled and the people were desolate and impoverished; Junli gathered soldiers, repaired weapons, and was deeply praised for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: War had not yet ended and the people were destitute. Junli gathered troops, repaired weapons, and was praised for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，累遷左戶尚書。

translations.literal: When Wendi succeeded to the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he rose to minister of the left household.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，為東陽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjia he became governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjia he became governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，以父憂去職，自請往荊州迎柩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he left office for his father's mourning and himself requested to go to Jingzhou to meet the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang he left office to mourn his father and asked to go to Jingzhou to meet the coffin.

sentences.zh: 朝議以在位重臣，難令出境，乃遣長兄君嚴往焉。

translations.literal: The court debated that as a weighty minister in office it was hard to let him leave the realm, and therefore sent his elder brother Junyan in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that as a senior minister in office he could not leave the realm, and sent his elder brother Junyan instead.

sentences.zh: 及還，將葬，詔贈巡侍中、領軍將軍，諡曰敬子。

translations.literal: When they returned and were about to bury him, an edict posthumously gave Xun Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Guards, with the posthumous name Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned for the burial, an edict posthumously honored Xun as attendant-in-chief and general of the guards, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 太建中，歷位太子詹事，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he passed through the posts of Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he served as tutor of the heir apparent and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以君理女為皇太子妃，賜爵望蔡縣侯，位侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan made Junli's daughter the crown prince's consort, granted the noble rank Marquis of Wangcai, and gave him the posts of Attendant-in-Chief and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan made Junli's daughter the crown prince's consort, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wangcai, and appointed him attendant-in-chief and right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈翊左將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰貞憲。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General of the Left Assistants, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Opening of an Office with Equipage equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as general of the left assistants and grand master with golden seal and office equal to the three excellencies, with the posthumous name Upright and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 君理弟君高、君公。

translations.literal: Junli's younger brothers were Jungao and Jungong.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's younger brothers were Jungao and Jungong.

sentences.zh: 君高字季高，少知名，性剛直，有吏能。

translations.literal: Jungao, style name Jigao, was known from youth, with a nature upright and firm and ability as an administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jungao, whose style name was Jigao, was known from youth. He was upright by nature and skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 位衛尉卿，平越中郎將、都督、廣州刺史，甚得人和。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Minister of the Guards, General Who Pacifies the Yue, commander, and governor of Guangzhou, and greatly won human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the guards, general who pacifies the Yue, commander, and governor of Guangzhou, and won great goodwill.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡祁子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Qizi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Qizi.

sentences.zh: 君公自梁元帝敗後，常在江陵。

translations.literal: Jungong, after Liang's Emperor Yuan was defeated, constantly remained at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated, Jungong remained at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，與蕭瓛、蕭岩叛隋歸陳，後主擢為太子詹事。

translations.literal: In Zhenming, with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan he rebelled against Sui and returned to Chen; the Later Lord promoted him to Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming he rebelled against Sui with Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan and returned to Chen. Houzhu promoted him to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 君公博學有才辯，善談論，後主深器之。

translations.literal: Jungong was broadly learned, talented in debate, skilled at discussion, and the Later Lord deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Jungong was learned and eloquent, skilled at discussion, and Houzhu valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，文帝以其叛亡，命斬于建康。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui; Emperor Wen, because of his rebellion and flight, ordered him beheaded at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui. Emperor Wen of Sui, because of his defection, ordered him beheaded at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 君理第五叔邁，亦方正有幹局，位通直散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was also upright and had administrative capacity; he held the post of Regular Attendant and attended the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Junli's fifth uncle Mai was also upright and capable. He served as regular attendant and attended the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 陸山才字孔章，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shancai, style name Kongzhang, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shancai, whose style name was Kongzhang, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖翁寶，梁尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wengbao was Director of the Water Bureau in the Secretariat under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wengbao had been director of the water bureau in the secretariat under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父泛，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Grand Master of Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan had been grand master of leisure.

sentences.zh: 山才倜儻，好尚文史，范陽張纘、纘弟綰並欽重之。

translations.literal: Shancai was free and bold, fond of literature and history; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and Zuan's younger brother Wan both greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shancai was bold and unconventional and loved literature and history. Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and his younger brother Wan both esteemed him highly.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，都督周文育出鎮南豫州，不知書疏，以山才為長史，政事悉以委之。

translations.literal: In Shaotai, the commander Zhou Wenyü went out to garrison South Yuzhou; not knowing letters and memorials, he made Shancai his chief secretary and entrusted all government affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai the commander Zhou Wenyü went out to garrison South Yuzhou. Unable to handle documents himself, he made Shancai his chief secretary and entrusted all affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 文育南討，克蕭勃，禽歐陽頠，計畫多出山才。

translations.literal: Wenyü campaigned south, overcame Xiao Bo, and captured Ouyang Yi; the plans mostly came from Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü campaigned south, defeated Xiao Bo, and captured Ouyang Yi. Most of the plans came from Shancai.

sentences.zh: 後文育重鎮豫章金口，山才復為鎮南長史、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Later Wenyü again garrisoned Jinkou in Yuzhang; Shancai again became chief secretary of the Southern Garrison and governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenyü again garrisoned Jinkou in Yuzhang. Shancai again served as chief secretary of the southern garrison and governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，曇朗囚山才等，送于王琳。

translations.literal: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and the others and sent them to Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü was killed by Xiong Tanlang. Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and the others and sent them to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 未至，而侯安都敗琳將常眾愛，由是山才獲反。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and thereby Shancai was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai, and Shancai was able to return.

sentences.zh: 累遷度支尚書，坐侍宴與蔡景曆言語過差，為有司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue; for sitting at a feast and speaking improperly with Cai Jingli, he was impeached by the authorities and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of revenue but was dismissed after speaking improperly with Cai Jingli at a feast.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍，遷西陽、武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant and moved to governor of the two commanderies of Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed regular attendant and governor of Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：趙知禮、蔡景曆屬陳武經綸之日，居文房書記之任，此乃宋、齊之初傅亮、王儉之職。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli belonged to the days when Chen Wu was laying out the state; they held the posts of secretaries in the literary chamber—this was the office of Fu Liang and Wang Jian at the beginning of Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli served during the days when Chen Wu was building the state, holding the posts of literary secretaries—the same offices Fu Liang and Wang Jian held at the beginning of Song and Qi.

sentences.zh: 若乃校其才用，理不同年，而卒能膺務濟時，蓋其遇也。

translations.literal: If one compares their talent and employment, reason says they were not of the same year, yet in the end they could undertake affairs and aid the times—this was their fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Compared in talent and employment, they were not equals, yet both could serve the times effectively—this was their good fortune.

sentences.zh: 希祥勞臣之子，才名自致，跡涉便佞，貞介所羞。

translations.literal: Xixiang, son of a meritorious minister, achieved fame by his own talent, but his conduct touched on flattery and advancement, which the upright despise.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang, son of a meritorious minister, won fame by his own talent, but his conduct touched on flattery, which the upright despise.

sentences.zh: 元饒始終任遇，無虧公道，名位自卒，其殆優乎。

translations.literal: Yuanrao from beginning to end received trust and favor without impairing public justice; his fame and rank ended with him—was he not perhaps superior?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrao enjoyed trust from beginning to end without compromising justice and died in honor—was he not perhaps the superior man?

sentences.zh: 子高權重為戮，亦其宜也。

translations.literal: Zigao, his authority weighty, was executed—this too was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's power was excessive and his execution was fitting.

sentences.zh: 華皎經綸雲始，既蹈元功，殷憂之辰，自同勁草，雖致奔敗，未足為非。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao from the beginning of laying out the state trod the original merit; in days of deep sorrow he was himself like tough grass; though he met defeat and flight, it was not enough to count as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao helped build the state from the beginning and shared in its founding merit. In days of deep trouble he stood firm as tough grass. Though he met defeat, that was not enough to condemn him.

sentences.zh: 師知送往多闕，見忌新主，謀人之義，可無慎哉；

translations.literal: Shizhi in sending off the departed had many lapses, was resented by the new ruler—in the meaning of plotting against others, could one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi had many lapses in the matter of the deposed emperor and was resented by the new ruler. In plotting against others, could one not be more cautious?

sentences.zh: 然晚遇誅夷，非其過也。

translations.literal: Yet meeting execution late in life was not his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his late execution was not his fault.

sentences.zh: 毛喜逢時遇主，好謀而成，見廢昏朝，不致公輔，惜矣。

translations.literal: Mao Xi met the time and encountered his lord, was fond of planning and achieved success, yet was cast aside by a benighted court and did not reach the highest offices—alas.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi met the right time and the right lord, planned well and succeeded, yet was cast aside by a benighted court and never reached the highest offices—a pity.

sentences.zh: 沈、陸所以見重，固亦雅望之所致焉。

translations.literal: The reason Shen and Lu were esteemed was indeed also brought about by their refined reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The esteem in which Shen and Lu were held was indeed due to their refined reputations.
